Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

can’t you …? phrase

an impatient request

also will you please …, would you mind …, can you …?, won’t you …?, can’t you be quiet?

classical

Plaut. Amph. 903b: Potin' ut abstineās manum?
Ter. Ad. 4.1.23: potin' ut dēsinās? (Lewis & Short)

Potin' ut …?

potin' (for potisne est, “is it possible”) with ut, or ut nē, and the subjunctive

can’t you …? will you kindly …?

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

A question in form, an order in fact: Lewis & Short renders potin' ut taceās? (Plaut. Poen. 4.2.94) simply “be silent”.

Examples

  • Potin' ut abstineās manum?

    Keep your hands off, can’t you?Plaut. Amph. 903b

  • Potin' ut mihi molestus nē sīs?

    Can’t you stop bothering me?Plaut. Cist. 465

See also please, come on!, stop it!, be quiet.

SourcesLewis & Short: potin'

Plautus, Amphitruo 903b; Cistellaria 465.
